title: Depression in Parkinson's
content: Depression can affect people living with Parkinson's disease and is considered an important non-movement symptom. Possible experiences include persistent sadness, loss of interest or pleasure, low motivation, changes in sleep or appetite, difficulty concentrating and feelings of hopelessness. Depression may result from a combination of psychological and biological factors and can also occur independently of Parkinson's disease. Symptoms of depression alone do not indicate Parkinson's disease. Persistent mood changes should be discussed with a qualified healthcare professional because depression can be treated. Expressions of self-harm, suicidal thoughts or immediate danger require urgent crisis or emergency support.
